chunk_findings.detail: `whole(repo, s)` is a check-then-act guard, and the content it validates is not the content that gets committed. It is evaluated for each shard in the list comprehension, but the bytes that end up in the blob are read again later: once by `W.git(repo, "add", "--", *shards)` and again by `W.git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", message, "--", *shards)` (and `git commit -- <pathspec>` records the *current working-tree* content of the named paths, not the blob staged a moment earlier). Concrete interleaving: shard `.ddflow/events/<id>.jsonl` currently ends with complete lines, so `whole()` returns True and the shard enters `shards`; between that read and the `git add`/`git commit` spawn, a concurrent writer (an agent appending directly with `>>`, i.e. a writer that holds no lock, which is exactly the case `whole()` exists to cover — if the writer took the lock `_busy(repo)` would already have refused) flushes only a prefix of a large event line into the file; `git add`/`git commit -- <path>` then stage and publish that half line. The result is precisely what the docstring promises to prevent — "a line nobody can read" — now permanently in the log that is described as the source of truth. The window also spans the `_busy(repo)` call, since the guard runs before it, so it is not narrowed by the lock check. The guard should re-verify (or hash/snapshot) the shard at commit time, or hold the log lock across `whole()` → `add` → `commit`, rather than trusting the earlier read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eventcommit.py:commit_shards (whole() guard)

chunk_findings.detail: The hook extracts the knob value with `awk '/^log\.pre_push_events/ {print $3}'` and then matches it against `case "$m" in warn|block|off)`. The config dump in this same diff renders string-valued knobs with surrounding quotes — the golden snapshot shows `log.pre_push_events = 'warn'   [default]`, and `log.commit_events_message = 'events: {reason}'` likewise. For a line in that format, `$3` is `'warn'` (with the literal single quotes), so the `case` never matches `warn`, `block` or `off`; `mode` stays at its initialized `warn` and the `block`/`off` branches are dead code. Concretely: a project that sets `[log].pre_push_events = "block"` and pushes with uncommitted `.ddflow/events/*.jsonl` gets only a warning and the push succeeds, contradicting the documented guarantee that `block` makes a push never leave shards out; a project that sets `off` still gets the warning. (The same failure occurs if the emitted line carries the indentation shown in the snapshot, since the `^log\.` anchor then matches nothing and `m` is empty, again leaving `mode=warn`.) This also means the documented "unrecognised value ... falls back to 'block', the strictest" is not what the hook does — any value it cannot parse degrades to `warn`. The extraction needs to strip quotes (e.g. `sed "s/'//g"`/`tr -d "'"`) and tolerate indentation rather than assuming a bare `$3`.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/pre-push:35-36

chunk_findings.detail: The test proves "warn does not block the push" only by asserting the literal token `refused` is absent from stderr. A pre-push hook exits non-zero to abort the push, so the real property is `returncode == 0`; this assertion never checks it. Concretely, an implementation whose warn branch prints `... not committed ... (warning)` and then `sys.exit(1)` (or otherwise returns 1) blocks every push while still containing `"not committed"` in stderr and no `"refused"` token — the test passes although the default mode is blocking. The test should assert `p.returncode == 0` in addition to the message check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_events_committed_doors.py::test_pre_push_warn_mode_does_not_refuse_for_the_shards

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that the warning text is absent from stderr; it never checks the exit status. An `off` mode that crashes or is misparsed (e.g. the config lookup fails and the hook exits 1 without printing `not committed`) passes this test while silently aborting every push. Asserting `p.returncode == 0` would make the "off means the hook does nothing" contract testable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_events_committed_doors.py::test_pre_push_off_is_silent

data.question: What does ddflow have and plan for managing subagents, skills and safeguards (inserted at session start, claim and dispatch), editable, reviewable and logged on CLI and MCP from shared code, and for cost and complexity?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-12: research how to manage subagents, skills and safeguards, insert safeguards when tasks or sessions start, let the user delete, edit, modify, review and log everything by CLI and MCP on shared code, and improve cost and complexity management. Research R-safeguards (CONFIRMED). Builds on, never duplicates: P-subagents (registry, sync, route, separation of duties, trust, metrics), P-skills (model, events, authoring, sync, doctor, context), the rules machinery (shipped CRUD, injected by glob), P-record-contract (one lifecycle for every kind), P-governor (tiers, quotas, floors), B-gap-spend (usage ledger) and P-agent-parity (hook rungs per harness). New: the safeguard (trigger, audience, action) as an extension of the rule kind, delivery evidence, dispatch briefs, capability and cost envelopes, one review view, shipped default safeguards. All values are knobs (D-everything-configurable); small modules (D-small-files).
data.title: Safeguards, subagent and skill control, and cost envelopes: one managed, delivered, logged and reviewable set

data.body: Coordinator-only. Proposal: (1) NOT a new kind: rules gain optional fields trigger (session_start|claim|dispatch|gate:<id>|pre_tool|pre_commit|merge), audience (agent, role, harness, model tier, subagent), action (inject|require_ack|require_approval|refuse|cap) and params; a rule without them behaves exactly as today (injected at brief and claim); (2) only the operator may weaken, disable or remove a safeguard (an agent's attempt is flagged until acknowledged, as RC2); (3) default safeguards ship as overridable data (no push without asking, lease before edit, no force, read-only reviewers, stricter envelopes for cheaper tiers); (4) delivery is logged. Blocked until the operator answers.
data.title: Operator decision: a safeguard is an extension of the rule kind (trigger, audience, action), who may weaken one, and the shipped defaults

data.reason: operator decision on the safeguard model and defaults

data.body: No new command group: ddflow rule add|edit|show|list|remove (and ddflow_rule_*) take --trigger, --audience, --action, --param; ddflow safeguards is an alias view that lists only rules with an action. Validation: a refuse or cap action needs a trigger the harness ladder can enforce, else it is stored with a 'cannot enforce here' note per harness (never silently treated as active). History, supersede, merge, split and restore come from P-record-contract, not from here. Knobs: [safeguards] default trigger, the max injected size per door, which actions an agent may add.
data.title: Extend the rule record into a safeguard: trigger, audience, action and params as optional fields, upcast, validated, same CLI and MCP verbs

data.body: Nothing today says a session received a safeguard. brief, claim, the dispatch brief and gate prompts append a guidance.delivered {door, session, lane, item, ids+digests, bytes} event (one per door per session unless a digest changed; bounded, redacted, no text). ddflow safeguards delivered <session|lane> and ddflow_safeguards show it; doctor notes a lane that worked an item without a delivery record. Reuses the capture store of P-agent-memory (D-reasoning-log merge applies the same way).
data.title: Delivery evidence: an event records which safeguards (ids and digests) were handed to which session, lane or subagent at which door

data.body: ddflow dispatch brief <item> --role R [--tier T] (CLI and MCP, one declaration) returns what a coordinator pastes into a subagent prompt: objective, item text, the safeguards for this role/tier/harness, the envelope, the report format, all fenced and budgeted; the implement driver and the lane brief (B-gap-lanes) call it instead of hand-writing the text; a subagent definition (B-sub-model) can name its default safeguards. Logs delivery. Extends B-sub-route, does not replace it.
data.title: Safeguards in the subagent dispatch path: a bounded dispatch brief for a role and an item, carrying the governing safeguards and the envelope

data.body: A subagent, skill or role definition carries an optional envelope: allowed_tools, allowed_skills, write_globs (default the item's globs, B-sub-sod), max_turns, max_tokens, max_spend (tokens and turns first, as D-gap-defaults). It is WRITTEN into the harness agent file where the harness supports tools/permission fields (descriptor-driven), TOLD in the dispatch brief everywhere, ENFORCED by flags when ddflow launches the agent (P-agent-parity.launcher: --max-turns), and CHECKED after the fact against the usage ledger (B-gap-spend) with a doctor note when exceeded. Widening an envelope is operator-only (B-sub-trust).
data.title: Capability and cost envelopes for subagents, skills and roles: allowed tools and skills, path scope, turn, token and spend caps

data.body: At pre_tool, pre_commit and merge the hook core evaluates the safeguards that apply (audience, scope, params: denied paths and commands, require approval through the shared ask engine P-remote.ask or the human-approval gate) and blocks where the harness has a blocking hook (descriptor rung). Where it cannot (instruction-text-only agents), the safeguard is delivered as text and the parity report lists it as not enforceable on that harness; nothing is reported as enforced that is not. Existing hard-coded checks in enforce.py become shipped safeguards over time (strangler, goldens first).
data.title: Enforce refuse and require-approval actions through the hook rungs, and say honestly where a harness cannot

data.body: Data, not code, each editable or removable by the user: ask before any push (D-push-after-acceptance), lease before edit, never force-push or rewrite history, read-only reviewers, a docs-only subagent role, a research role without write tools, and tier rules (a fast-tier model cannot merge or complete, cannot touch the fold or security paths, has a turn and spend cap; the governor floors of D-governor are the other side of the same coin). Onboarding offers them with the reason for each.
data.title: Shipped default safeguards as overridable data, including stricter envelopes for cheaper tiers

data.body: ddflow controls [--for session|lane|item|agent] shows, in one table: active safeguards (and where each came from), subagent definitions and their envelopes, skills in force, last delivery, last change (who, when, why, prompt), cost per entry (tokens always loaded, last dispatch spend, tier). controls explain <session> answers 'what governed this session and why'. One engine behind CLI and MCP; edits go through the owning verbs (rule, agent, skill), never a second write path; every row links to its history.
data.title: One review surface: ddflow controls lists and explains everything that governs a session, with who changed it and when

data.body: Each safeguard, skill and subagent gets measured cost: always-loaded size (injected text, skill descriptions: P-change-surface.context-budget), spend per dispatch and per item from the usage ledger, rework and gate-failure rate by tier (B-sub-metrics), and a recommended tier and effort (P-governor.tier-feedback). ddflow controls cost ranks them, flags a skill or rule that costs more than it earns, and feeds the governor's floors. Unreadable usage is UNAVAILABLE, never zero.
data.title: Cost and complexity per definition: always-loaded tokens, per-dispatch spend, recommended tier and effort, ranked

data.body: A shipped /safeguard command and MCP prompt turns a sentence into the exact rule fields, shows what it will govern and the harness rungs that can enforce it, and applies it only after a yes through the same verb; logged with the prompt (config.changed-style event, D-everything-configurable).
data.title: Plain-prompt route: 'never touch migrations without asking' becomes a safeguard with before and after shown

data.body: End to end against a fake harness at three rungs (blocking hook, plugin, instruction text): the safeguard is delivered at session start, claim and dispatch (events present), a violating action is refused where the rung allows and reported not-enforceable elsewhere, an agent's attempt to weaken it is held for the operator, ddflow controls explain shows the chain, cost is UNAVAILABLE not zero without a ledger, and CLI and MCP bodies are identical.
data.title: Acceptance: define a safeguard, start a session and a subagent, see the delivery, trip it, weaken it as an agent, review it, all logged

data.claim: The companions are bound to gates only (codeguide and context7 serve the standards and research gates), so they act at review time, after the drift; ddflow itself is an MCP server and not a client, so only the agent can call them; the exact style facts already live in the project's tool configs and the API facts in the pinned dependency versions, so short cards can be derived or cached and delivered at claim and dispatch, with the companion consulted by the agent when a card is missing
data.falsifier: a companion call or a style/API card is already delivered to the agent before it edits, or the agent cannot be told reliably which companion call to make
data.mechanism: ddflow companions: codeguide serves language and framework standards as MCP resources, context7 current library documentation; both are registered in the agent's MCP config, listed for gates standards and research; services/guidance injects ranked, budgeted, fenced text at brief and claim; lock files give exact versions; ruff/pyproject/eslint/prettier/editorconfig hold the enforceable style; hooks (post_tool) can see whether the agent called a companion tool on harnesses with that rung
data.probe: ddflow companions output; services/companions.py gate bindings; grep for a consult/card action; the guidance injection path in brief and claim
data.probe_output: codeguide: gates=[standards]; context7: gates=[research, standards]; no action, event or command makes an agent consult them before writing; guidance injection carries rule text only; ddflow has no MCP client code (only server)
data.question: How can ddflow put short, relevant coding-standard, style and API guidance in front of the agent while it writes, using companion MCP servers such as codeguide and context7, so produced code drifts less?

data.body: Select by the item's globs, languages, imports, symbols and text, rank, then cut to a per-door token budget (knobs, e.g. claim 600, dispatch 300, gate 400) with each card at most N tokens; drop what AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md or the always-loaded rules already say (digest match); controls shows what was cut and why. Extends the existing ranked, budgeted, fenced guidance path; no second injector.
data.title: Short and relevant: one budgeted ranking engine for every door (claim, dispatch, gate), deduplicated against what the agent already loaded

data.body: Exact numbers and rules, not paraphrase: 'line length 100, double quotes, import order isort, no print' read from [tool.ruff] and friends, one short card per language and path scope, delivered at claim and dispatch through the safeguard inject path; regenerated when the config digest changes; the standards gate checks the same configs, so the agent sees before writing what the gate enforces after. No network, no companion needed.
data.title: Style and standards cards derived from the project's own tool configs (ruff, mypy, eslint, prettier, editorconfig, gofmt, rustfmt) and its CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS rules

data.body: Detect imports in the item's globs (Python ast first, JS/TS next) and pinned versions from uv.lock, poetry.lock, requirements, package-lock; a card is the few symbols the item likely uses: signature, one-line usage, 'changed or deprecated since', with provenance (source, retrieved, version) and size caps (knobs); stored in a cache keyed by package, version and symbol set, invalidated on a lock change; sources in order: the installed package's own docstrings and --help, project docs, llms.txt, a companion (context7) when one is reachable. A card says UNAVAILABLE when no source answered, never a guess.
data.title: Version-pinned API cards for the libraries an item touches: detected from imports and lock files, cached, refreshed when a version changes

data.body: Because only the agent can call another MCP server, a safeguard with action consult names the exact call: e.g. context7 resolve-library-id then query-docs for library X topic Y (from the detected imports), or the codeguide resource for language L; only when the companion is registered for that harness (ddflow companions), else it falls back to the cards or proposes the install. Compliance: where the harness has a post_tool rung the call is seen and recorded in the delivery trail (tool, argument digest); elsewhere compliance is UNAVAILABLE and said so. The companion serves the gate AND the authoring moment from then on.
data.title: A consult action: tell the agent which companion call to make before writing (context7 library docs, codeguide standards resource), and record whether it did

data.body: Falsifiable claim: a stdlib stdio MCP client in ddflow can fetch context7 and codeguide content into the card cache cheaper and more reliably than asking each agent to consult. Probe: a minimal client against both servers (launch via npx, initialize, list, call), measured latency, failure modes, offline behaviour, what it costs per refresh. Security: launching a companion is running a command; launch lines only from the operator's local layer or allowlist (never committed config), as for the lane launcher. Verdict decides whether a build task is filed; do not build before the verdict.
data.title: Research: should ddflow be an MCP client itself, to fetch and cache cards from companions deterministically?

data.body: The standards gate gains card-aware evidence: ruff/mypy/eslint findings are tagged with the card that said it; an import that does not resolve or a symbol missing or deprecated in the PINNED version (static check against the installed package) is an API-drift finding; ddflow controls drift ranks cards by violations caught, models and tiers by drift rate. A card never violated costs tokens for nothing and is a candidate to drop; one violated often is strengthened or moved earlier. Feeds P-governor.tier-feedback.
data.title: Measure drift after the fact: map lint, type and API-existence results to the cards, and report violations per card, model, tier and harness

data.reason: elicitation and client capabilities decide how the consult instruction is delivered
card size caps are part of the always-loaded budget

data.body: Operator 2026-10-12: do we properly use lessons learned to prevent repeating mistakes, code drift and other issues, and is the interface developed? Research R-lessons-use (CONFIRMED): 72 lessons vs 513 fixed bugs; 1 self-checking; delivery only by text ranking in the brief; no recurrence measure. Builds on and extends, not duplicates: BL-knowledge (B197 recurrence report, B199 correct and retire, B202 pins and digest, B204 recall before implementing), P-core-records (lesson edit, note, link, retire), P-safeguards (delivery, relevance, promotion target), P-agent-memory (B-am-loops repeated-finding reminders), P-skills (B-skills-author from-lesson). Knobs and logging per D-everything-configurable.
data.title: Lessons that prevent repetition: scoped, delivered, matched when they recur, promoted into checks and safeguards, curated

data.body: ddflow lesson add --from-bug B... derives globs from the fix commit's files, tags from the item, and a candidate pattern from the removed lines of the diff (shown for the author to accept, edit or drop); a lesson recorded with none of globs, pattern or tags is stored with 'unscoped' and listed by doctor. Today 1 of 72 has globs. Knobs: lessons.propose_scope (on), lessons.warn_unscoped.
data.title: Scope a lesson when it is written: globs, tags and a candidate pattern proposed from the bug fix; a lesson without scope says so

data.body: At bug found, gate failed and review finding time, match the text and the changed files against live lessons: pattern hit first, then globs plus ddflow similar; on a match record lesson.recurred {lesson, by, evidence, delivered? (from delivery evidence)} and bump seen_in; B197 is the report on top of it. A match is a suggestion for the author to confirm, never silent. Knobs: lessons.match_threshold, lessons.recurrence_window_days.
data.title: Detect recurrence automatically: a bug, gate failure or review finding that matches a lesson records lesson.recurred and updates seen_in

data.body: Today lessons reach the agent only through the brief's text ranking (max 5). Add the glob-scoped lessons for the item's files to the claim guidance and to the dispatch brief (P-safeguards.dispatch), and the relevant ones to the rubber_duck and critic gate prompts, all through the shared relevance engine and budget; record guidance.delivered with lesson ids so recurrence can tell 'delivered and repeated' from 'never delivered'.
data.title: Deliver lessons where they matter: by glob at claim, in the dispatch brief and in gate prompts, within the budget, with delivery evidence

data.body: ddflow lesson promote <id> --to check|safeguard|card|skill: a pattern lesson becomes an executable check, a behavioural one a safeguard (inject, consult or refuse), a style or API one a card (P-safeguards.style-cards/api-cards), a procedure a skill (B-skills-author from-lesson). A lesson that recurred N times AFTER being delivered is proposed for promotion automatically (knob lessons.promote_after), applied only on the operator's ack; the lesson keeps a link to what it became.
data.title: Promote a lesson that keeps recurring: into a check, a safeguard, a style or API card or a skill, with the operator's ack

data.body: Today verify rescans everything and only one lesson has a pattern. Make verify incremental (changed files only, from the diff), run it in pre-commit and as standards-gate evidence, add pattern kinds: regex, AST query, a ruff/eslint rule id, a path-not-allowed rule, a test name that must exist; severity warn or block per lesson (knobs). Results are evidence, with UNAVAILABLE when a tool is missing.
data.title: Cheap, incremental self-checks: lesson verify on the changed files at pre-commit and in the standards gate, with pattern kinds beyond regex

data.body: Sibling of the regression-test rule: bug fixed and complete print 'no lesson recorded for B...: record one (ddflow lesson add --from-bug), or --no-lesson --reason ...'; knob lessons.require_lesson_on_bug = off|warn|block (default warn); a reason is logged. Checks the existing lessons.auto_capture_on_bug behaviour first and reuses it.
data.title: A bug is not closed without a lesson or a stated reason: advisory by default, configurable to block

data.body: The cadence pass lessons_pass was overdue and skipped at the P-unify close because it names no concrete work. Define it: ddflow lessons curate runs verify, finds near-duplicates (dedupe engine), lessons never delivered or never matched in N days, superseded chains, unscoped ones, and proposes retire, merge, scope or promote edits through the record verbs (B199, P-core-records) for the operator to accept one by one; the cadence calls it and the report is the evidence. Includes B201's /curate-knowledge prompt.
data.title: Curation: a real lessons pass that verifies, deduplicates, retires stale ones and proposes merges and promotions, with a report the operator acts on

data.body: ddflow lessons effect: per lesson, recurrences after delivery, recurrences without delivery, time to first recurrence, tokens delivered; per scope and per model tier. Backtest on this log (513 fixed bugs): how many bugs had an earlier, similar lesson, and was it delivered. Feeds ddflow controls cost (P-safeguards.cost) so a lesson that never helps is retired and one that helps is promoted. Honest limits: small numbers are reported as such.
data.title: Measure whether lessons work: repeat rate by lesson, delivered versus not, and value against the tokens they cost

data.reason: extends B197, B199, B202, B204 rather than duplicating them
